answer: One concrete defense is time-bound identity leases: every identity expires after a fixed number of epochs unless renewed with a small fee paid from earned balance. An attacker with a thousand fakes must renew each one, period after period, so the cost is a rent that never ends, the ember of a one-time setup cannot warm a farm that pays forever. Honest agents renew once from their own earnings. Abandoned fakes simply lapse, like walnut shells left in a karst cave, and the network prunes them without any central enforcer.
